selected_records.title: Behavioral Safety Assessment towards Large-scale Deployment of Autonomous Vehicles, Part II: Assessment Results

article.body:
Autonomous Vehicle Behavioral Safety Assessment Results

A third-party testing initiative for evaluating autonomous vehicle (AV) behavioral safety has been validated using Autoware.Universe, an open-source Level 4 Automated Driving System (ADS). The system was tested both in simulated environments and on the physical test track at the University of Michigan's Mcity Testing Facility. The results indicate that Autoware.Universe possesses 6 out of 14 behavioral competencies and exhibited a crash rate of 3.01x10^-3 crashes per mile, approximately 1,000 times higher than the average human driver crash rate. During the tests, unknown unsafe scenarios for Autoware.Universe were uncovered, underscoring the necessity of behavioral safety evaluations for improving AV safety performance prior to widespread public deployment. No specific regulatory or commercial implications were reported in the study.
